name: rest-api
title: REST API
description: A REST API built with Hono and zod whose customers and orders live in your own Supabase tables — one Function, six routes, rolled back as one unit.

env.description: Your Supabase project's URL, e.g. https://abcdefghijklmnop.supabase.co. Setting it opens that one host to your App's outbound calls. Leave it blank to deploy first: every route then answers 503 until it is set.
env.where_to_find: Supabase → your project → Project Settings → Data API → Project URL. The Connect button at the top of the project shows it too.

env.description: The key the Function reads and writes with. It must be the secret key: schema.sql turns on row-level security with no policy, so the publishable key can do nothing.
env.where_to_find: Supabase → your project → Project Settings → API Keys → Secret keys. It starts with sb_secret_. Keep it on the server: it skips every policy.

post_deploy:
Your API is live at {{url}}

If you left the two Supabase values blank, every route answers 503 for now. To
connect it, in this order:
  1. Create a project at https://supabase.com/dashboard.
  2. Open its SQL Editor, paste in schema.sql from this project, and run it. That
     creates the customers and orders tables, and one customer to start with.
  3. Set the project URL (Project Settings → Data API). This also opens that one
     host to your App's outbound calls:
       wawesome env set SUPABASE_URL https://<project-ref>.supabase.co
  4. Set the secret key (Project Settings → API Keys):
       wawesome env set SUPABASE_KEY sb_secret_... --secret

Then try it:
  curl {{url}}
  curl -X POST {{url}} -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Nadia Petrova","email":"nadia@example.com"}'
  curl {{url}}/<id>/orders

Next:
  - The routes are in src/index.ts. The shape of a customer is the zod schema at
    the top of it.
  - Watch requests land as they happen:
      wawesome logs --follow
  - Every route is public. Authentication is yours to add.
